name: AHAWR: OpenAI Codex CLI as a second executor in claude-runner
objective:
Repository D:\n8n is the mission's WORKING DIRECTORY. claude-runner (claude-runner/) runs the Claude Code CLI (2.1.283) headless behind the /v1/runs API that the n8n Run Manager uses; a run's provider selects a provider block (CLAUDE_RUNNER_PROVIDER_<NAME>__<VAR>), and the dashboard reads the runner's events (steps with tokens and timings, tool calls and results, text, thinking, compactions).

GOAL: add the OpenAI Codex CLI (npm @openai/codex, pin a version, 0.159.0 at the time of writing) as a second executor, chosen per provider block (e.g. CLAUDE_RUNNER_PROVIDER_<NAME>__ENGINE=codex), so a role can run on Codex without changing the n8n workflows. Known from the Codex docs (verify each against the pinned CLI: `codex exec --help`, `codex exec resume --help`, the package's docs/config schema):
- `codex exec --json "<prompt>"` prints JSON Lines events: thread.started (session id), turn.started, turn.completed (usage: input_tokens, cached_input_tokens, output_tokens, reasoning_output_tokens), turn.failed, item.started / item.completed (agent messages, reasoning, command executions, file changes, MCP tool calls, plan updates); `-o/--output-last-message`; `--output-schema`.
- `codex exec resume <SESSION_ID> "<prompt>"` continues a session.
- `--sandbox read-only | workspace-write | danger-full-access`; `approval_policy`; `permissions.<name>.filesystem.<path>` (read/write/deny); `shell_environment_policy` (exclude, filters).
- config.toml: `model_providers.<id>` (base_url, wire_api = "responses" only - chat completions support was removed, env_key, http_headers, request_max_retries, stream_idle_timeout_ms), `model_context_window`, `model_auto_compact_token_limit`, `compact_prompt` / `experimental_compact_prompt_file`, `tool_output_token_limit`, `model_instructions_file`, `project_doc_fallback_filenames`, `hooks` (SessionStart, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PreCompact, PostCompact, Stop, ...).
- Auth: CODEX_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY for OpenAI models. For the local model the llama.cpp build of this stack serves the OpenAI Responses API at /v1/responses (llama-server, host.docker.internal:8080), so Codex can talk to llama-server directly without LiteLLM.

Implement in claude-runner: the engine switch; building the codex command and a per-run CODEX_HOME with a generated config.toml (provider, context window 65536 and auto-compact limit for the local model, short compaction prompt like the Claude PreCompact instructions, tool output limit, sandbox per role: Architect/Reviewer read-only, Worker able to edit the mission folder; deny reading .env files except .env.example; no secrets in the shell environment); capturing the session id and resuming; mapping Codex events to the runner's event entries so the dashboard shows steps, tool calls and usage; the final message as the run result; failure mapping (transient vs permanent, context overflow); a cost estimate from a configurable price table (Codex reports no cost); what POST /v1/sessions/{id}/compact does for a Codex session (a real compaction if the CLI supports one headless, otherwise a documented fallback such as a low auto-compact limit or the digest handoff). Claude Code runs must behave exactly as before.
rules_json: ["Change only: claude-runner/src, claude-runner/tests, claude-runner/README.md, claude-runner/Dockerfile, claude-runner/pyproject.toml, .env.example, docs/*.md, CHANGELOG.md", "Claude Code behaviour stays unchanged; the Codex engine is off unless a provider block selects it", "Do NOT restart, rebuild or stop claude-runner, ahawr-litellm, llama-cpp-server or n8n; do not send requests to llama-server or LiteLLM (this mission runs on that model); do not import workflows. List the apply commands in the report instead", "Tests use a fake codex executable (like tests/fake_claude.py) that replays recorded JSONL; base the recorded events on the pinned CLI's real output format - install the pinned package into a temporary directory outside the repository (npm install --prefix /tmp/codex-cli @openai/codex@<version>) and use its --help output and bundled docs/schemas; mark anything not confirmed there as a hypothesis", "No real OpenAI API calls and no API keys: do not read or change .env or keys, do not print environment variables", "pytest, ruff check, ruff format --check and mypy src for claude-runner pass (the tools are in the runner image); quote their output", "Read large files by line range: grep -n | head and Read with offset/limit; quote at most ~30 lines of any output in the report", "Do not run git commit, push, stash, checkout or reset"]
acceptance_criteria_json: ["A provider block can select the Codex engine; with no such setting every run uses Claude Code exactly as before (existing tests pass unchanged)", "Codex runs: command and generated config.toml (provider with wire_api responses, context window, auto-compact limit, compaction prompt, tool output limit, sandbox per role, .env deny, environment policy) are built and covered by tests", "Session id is captured from the event stream and a later run resumes it with codex exec resume; covered by tests", "Codex JSONL events become runner events (steps with usage, tool calls with results, messages, reasoning, compactions if reported) and the final message becomes the run result; covered by tests with recorded events", "Failure mapping (transient, permanent, context overflow) and the /v1/sessions/{id}/compact behaviour for Codex are implemented or documented with the reason", "Cost estimate for Codex runs from a configurable price table", "Dockerfile can install a pinned Codex CLI (build argument), README and .env.example document the setup for OpenAI models and for the local llama-server via /v1/responses", "pytest, ruff check, ruff format --check and mypy pass; the final report lists changed files, test output, apply commands and open questions"]
